question: What does dietary diversity primarily involve consuming?

options.A: Large quantities of a single local staple food
options.B: A wide variety of foods from different groups
options.C: Only protein-rich foods during every single meal
options.D: Strictly imported food items to ensure safety

explanation: Dietary diversity focuses on eating multiple different food groups rather than relying on just one item. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h1)

question: Why is relying solely on a single staple food problematic for health?

options.A: It fails to provide all essential vitamins and minerals
options.B: It causes immediate total digestive system failure
options.C: It always introduces dangerous toxins into the body
options.D: It contains no carbohydrates or energy for daily work

explanation: Staples supply energy but lack the complete micronutrient profile needed for full health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h1)

question: Which food category do cassava and yam belong to in nutritional assessments?
explanation: Roots, tubers, and cereals are classified as starchy staples providing major energy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: Fluted pumpkin leaves and jute mallow are examples of which food group?
explanation: These local greens are rich sources of essential vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: What does the term hidden hunger refer to in community nutrition?

options.A: Eating secretly between meals due to psychological stress
options.B: Micronutrient deficiencies despite adequate daily calorie intake
options.C: Unrecognized food allergies triggered by processed snacks
options.D: Severe starvation caused by a complete lack of food

explanation: People can eat enough food to stop feeling hungry while still lacking vital vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: Which specific micronutrients are most commonly deficient in diets lacking diversity?
explanation: These specific minerals and vitamins are frequently missing when diets rely on single staples. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: What timeframe do standard dietary diversity assessment tools typically evaluate?
explanation: A 24-hour recall period is standard for measuring recent food group consumption accurately. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: What does a low dietary diversity score indicate during a community health assessment?

options.A: High risk for micronutrient deficiencies and poor nutrition
options.C: Adequate intake of all essential vitamins and minerals
options.D: Excessive consumption of animal protein products

explanation: Fewer food groups consumed point directly to a lower intake of essential nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: Which factor most directly limits low-income families from buying diverse foods?

options.A: Universal laws banning the sale of local crops
options.B: A complete absence of cooking utensils in homes
options.C: Personal preference for eating only processed foods
options.D: Poverty and limited household purchasing power

explanation: Financial constraints make expensive nutrient-dense foods out of reach for poor households. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: How do cultural taboos negatively impact nutritional status in some communities?

options.A: By eliminating the need for clean drinking water sources
options.B: By forcing families to consume excessive amounts of vegetables
options.C: By restricting pregnant women from eating certain nutritious foods
options.D: By encouraging the overproduction of local staple crops

explanation: Cultural beliefs can prevent vulnerable groups from consuming available high-quality proteins. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: What is a direct health consequence of poor dietary diversity in young children?

options.C: Enhanced resistance to all infectious diseases
options.D: Rapid increase in bone mineral density

explanation: Lack of diverse nutrients stunts physical growth and slows brain development in early life. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)

question: Which complication is a pregnant woman with a monotonous diet most likely to face?

options.A: Rapid weight gain from fat accumulation
options.B: Increased bone strength and high energy
options.C: Excessive levels of vitamins and minerals
options.D: Anemia and low birth weight infants

explanation: Poor nutrient intake during pregnancy frequently leads to maternal anemia and vulnerable newborns. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)

question: What practical activity can a nurse encourage families to adopt to improve vegetable access?

options.A: Eliminating vegetables entirely from daily meal plans
options.B: Starting small home gardens or backyard farming
options.C: Importing expensive foreign produce from supermarkets
options.D: Relying solely on canned food items from abroad

explanation: Home gardening provides a reliable, low-cost source of fresh micronutrients for households. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h7)

question: Why is community outreach during clinic visits important for nutrition promotion?

options.A: It replaces the need for medical checkups and diagnostics
options.B: It allows nurses to educate mothers on combining local foods
options.C: It forces community members to change their cultural heritage
options.D: It guarantees that all patients receive financial grants

explanation: Clinic visits provide a direct platform to teach practical meal planning using accessible ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h7)
